purpose: Compare external standards and authorization/provenance approaches against AETHER X Semantic Trust Chain without converting research findings into features or authority.
core_semantic_chain: EVIDENCE -> DECISION -> AUTHORITY -> EXECUTION -> VERIFICATION -> VERIFIED OUTCOME
implementation_rule: INTEROPERATE WHERE POSSIBLE — DIFFERENTIATE WHERE VALUABLE

rows.what_it_solves: Standard attestation envelope binding one or more artifact subjects by name/digest to typed predicates and signatures.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Semantic separation of evidence, decision, authority, execution, verification, and verified outcome with provenance and historical/current truth boundaries.
rows.semantic_overlap: Artifact identity, provenance statements, signed evidence transport.
rows.missing_capability: No explicit generic import/export contract for representing AETHER evidence or verification facts as in-toto attestations while preserving AETHER semantic type boundaries.
rows.mapping: in-toto subject -> external artifact identity; predicate -> standard provenance or bounded AETHER evidence payload/reference; signer identity -> evidence source provenance. Imported attestation is Evidence unless an explicit AETHER rule creates another typed record.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: High if a signed attestation is interpreted as truth, decision, authority, or verified outcome merely because it is signed.
rows.authority_boundary: Signature authenticates an issuer statement; it does not grant AETHER authority or execution capability.
rows.reason: Define semantics first; runtime adapter would become an interoperability contract.

rows.what_it_solves: Supply-chain security levels plus build/source provenance and verification-summary attestation patterns.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Evidence lineage, verification records, current-vs-historical state, bounded acceptance semantics, and externally verifiable artifacts.
rows.semantic_overlap: Provenance, artifact/source identity, verification evidence, immutable revision references.
rows.missing_capability: No standard SLSA provenance/VSA consume-or-emit mapping into AETHER typed evidence and verification records.
rows.mapping: SLSA provenance -> Evidence about source/build process; SLSA VSA -> Evidence of an external verifier assessment. AETHER Verification may validate the attestation and its policy relevance; AETHER Verified Outcome remains separate.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: High if a SLSA level or VSA is treated as product correctness, security approval, or AETHER verified outcome.
rows.authority_boundary: SLSA provenance/levels do not create AETHER authority, release authority, or acceptance.
rows.reason: Candidate contract requires explicit semantic mapping and independent review before affecting Core semantics.

rows.version_status: Current PyPA specification originally defined by PEP 740
rows.what_it_solves: Distribution-index hosted attestations with in-toto subject filename and SHA-256 binding plus supported predicate types.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Current package identity binding, deterministic candidate hashes, evaluator handoff identity, historical evidence immutability.
rows.semantic_overlap: Exact artifact identity and provenance attachment for Python distributions.
rows.missing_capability: No authorized-index attestation retrieval/verification evidence path; current project only has local/current candidate identity validation and publication remains unauthorized.
rows.mapping: distribution filename+SHA-256 -> AETHER external artifact identity; hosted attestation verification -> Evidence; signing certificate identity -> provenance source; transparency entries -> optional supporting evidence.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: Medium-high if index-hosted attestation availability is interpreted as publication approval, human evaluation, security approval, or verified outcome.
rows.authority_boundary: Attestation verification proves binding/signing properties; publication, release, and AETHER authority remain separate.
rows.reason: External-index interaction is currently authority-gated; offline mapping can follow after semantic contract review.

rows.what_it_solves: Interoperable PDP-to-PEP authorization request/decision API using Subject, Resource, Action, Context, and boolean Decision.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Decision provenance, explicit authority grants, bounded agent authority, separation of authority from capability and execution.
rows.semantic_overlap: Authorization decision context and externally sourced allow/deny decision.
rows.missing_capability: No explicit mapping contract between AuthZEN information model and AETHER decision/authority records.
rows.mapping: AuthZEN Subject/Resource/Action/Context -> bounded external authorization evaluation context. AuthZEN Decision -> external authorization decision record/evidence that may inform AETHER decision processing. It MUST NOT directly create an AETHER authority grant.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: Critical if AuthZEN decision=true is promoted to AETHER Authority or capability without an explicit authority record and policy boundary.
rows.authority_boundary: PDP decision != AETHER authority. Deny must fail closed; allow remains insufficient for execution unless AETHER authority and capability checks also pass.
rows.reason: The first adapter contract would affect Core decision/authority semantics and therefore is an Oversight trigger.

rows.what_it_solves: Signed Statements, transparency registration, receipts, append-only/non-equivocating statement history, and auditability.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Evidence provenance, historical immutability semantics, verification records, temporal knowledge, and typed distinction between evidence and verified outcome.
rows.semantic_overlap: Statement provenance, historicity, artifact linking, third-party audit evidence.
rows.missing_capability: No SCITT Signed Statement/Receipt import/export mapping for AETHER evidence and verification records.
rows.mapping: SCITT Signed Statement -> Evidence envelope; iss -> evidence issuer identity; sub -> subject/artifact grouping identity; Receipt -> Evidence that a statement was registered in a transparency service; AETHER Verification may verify receipt/signature and record result.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: Critical if receipt/inclusion is treated as statement accuracy, AETHER verification, acceptance, or authority.
rows.authority_boundary: SCITT registration proves issuer statement registration and transparency properties; it does not prove the statement is true and does not grant AETHER authority.
rows.reason: Use external transparency services if needed; do not build a custom ledger.

rows.what_it_solves: Policy evaluation over principal/action/resource/context with Allow/Deny decisions and explicit policy semantics.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Authority lifecycle, bounded agent authority, execution gating, provenance, verification, and semantic trust chain.
rows.semantic_overlap: External policy decision and contextual authorization enforcement.
rows.missing_capability: No adapter contract for using Cedar as an external PDP/enforcement backend under AETHER authority constraints.
rows.mapping: AETHER bounded actor/action/resource/context -> Cedar PARC request; Cedar Allow/Deny -> external authorization decision evidence. AETHER authority grant and capability remain independently required.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: High if Cedar Allow becomes authority or if contextual policy data is accepted without point-in-time provenance.
rows.authority_boundary: Cedar decides under Cedar policy; AETHER decides whether that decision is admissible and whether separate AETHER authority/capability permits execution.
rows.reason: Do not build a custom generic policy language; backend adapter only if a concrete execution path requires it.

rows.what_it_solves: Relationship-based authorization using authorization models, relationship tuples, contextual tuples, and Check decisions.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Explicit authority semantics, bounded delegation, point-in-time knowledge, provenance, and execution/verification separation.
rows.semantic_overlap: Relationship/capability facts and external authorization checks.
rows.missing_capability: No adapter contract for treating OpenFGA relationship data/check results as external evidence without conflating them with authority.
rows.mapping: relationship tuples/model ID -> point-in-time external authorization evidence; Check allowed -> external decision evidence. Model ID must be preserved to avoid latest-model ambiguity.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: High if relationship existence or allowed=true becomes AETHER authority, or if model version is omitted and historical decisions cannot be reproduced.
rows.authority_boundary: OpenFGA relation/check != AETHER authority grant. AETHER remains the semantic authority layer and may use OpenFGA as a backend.
rows.reason: No ReBAC engine should be rebuilt in AETHER; adapter only when a concrete use case proves value.

rows.version_status: Active Internet-Drafts; workload credentials -02 July 2026; architecture/workload identity work in progress
rows.what_it_solves: Workload identity, credentials, proof-of-possession patterns, trust-domain scoped workload identifiers, and workload-to-workload authentication.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Agent authority, bounded execution authority, provenance, and semantic separation between actor identity, authority, capability, and outcome.
rows.semantic_overlap: Authenticated workload/agent identity and delegated execution context.
rows.missing_capability: No workload identity integration contract; stable standards are not yet available.
rows.mapping: Future WIMSE workload identifier/credential -> authenticated actor/workload identity evidence; proof-of-possession -> capability-to-present identity evidence. Neither creates AETHER authority.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: High if authenticated workload identity is interpreted as authorization or agent authority.
rows.authority_boundary: Identity != Authority; proof of possession != execution permission.
rows.reason: Core must not depend on unstable drafts.

rows.version_status: draft-ietf-oauth-transaction-tokens-11 / WG Last Call / latest revision July 30 2026
rows.what_it_solves: Short-lived transaction-scoped authorization context propagation across workload call chains, including subject, workload, scope/purpose, and request context.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Bounded authority/delegation semantics, agent authority, explicit execution boundaries, provenance, and verification.
rows.semantic_overlap: Bounded transaction intent/context and call-chain propagation.
rows.missing_capability: No stable token mapping for AETHER execution authority/context; base specification is still an Internet-Draft.
rows.mapping: Future transaction token claims -> external execution-context evidence. AETHER authority identifiers may be referenced but must not be synthesized from token scope or subject claims.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: Critical if possession of a transaction token is treated as the AETHER authority record itself or if scope expansion occurs across token replacement.
rows.authority_boundary: Transaction context != AETHER authority; token possession != capability beyond explicitly bounded execution checks.
rows.reason: Track until standard stabilizes; no Core dependency on draft.

rows.what_it_solves: Agent context propagation using actor/principal semantics on top of transaction tokens.
rows.what_aether_already_solves: Agent Authority with explicit separation of principal, delegate/agent, authority, capability, and execution.
rows.semantic_overlap: Principal-vs-agent actor identity and delegated execution context.
rows.missing_capability: No stable standard mapping and no reason to replace AETHER Agent Authority with token claims.
rows.mapping: Future act/sub claims -> actor/principal identity evidence only; AETHER Agent Authority record remains the source of bounded authority semantics.
rows.loss_of_meaning_risk: Critical if act/sub presence is interpreted as delegation authorization.
rows.authority_boundary: Actor/principal identity context != delegation grant or capability.

research_conclusions.highest_candidate_gap: A standard interoperability contract is absent for mapping external provenance/authorization/transparency facts into AETHER typed records without semantic promotion.
research_conclusions.smallest_next_integration_candidate: A read-only, offline in-toto/SLSA attestation mapping profile that imports artifact provenance as Evidence only and exports AETHER evidence references without creating Decision, Authority, or Verified Outcome.
research_conclusions.oversight_trigger: The candidate mapping profile would be a proposed interoperability contract touching Core semantic boundaries and must be independently reviewed before runtime implementation or promotion.
explicit_non_goals: cryptographic subsystem built merely to avoid existing standards
